patches.name: Network Request
patches.statusReason: In the web player, browsers enforce CORS, block http:// URLs from https pages, and forbid some headers; the desktop app sends requests without those limits.
patches.summary: Loads JSON, text, images, video, or sound from a URL when it gets a pulse, and reports loading and errors.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Network Request loads data from the internet when **Request** gets a pulse (a signal that's on for one frame). Nothing is sent until then, so changing the URL alone doesn't reload anything.

- **URL** is the address to load, starting with `https://`.
- **Method** is usually GET to read data. Use POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE to send data, with **Body** holding the JSON to send.
- **URL Parameters** and **Headers** are JSON objects added to the request, such as `{"q": "shoes"}` or an `Authorization` header.
- Right-click to choose what **Result** holds: JSON (the default), Text, Image, Video, or Sound.
- **Loading** is true while the request runs. **Finished** pulses when it ends, successfully or not.
- **Error** turns on when something went wrong, and **Error Message** says why in plain words. A failed request keeps the last good Result on screen.

## Tips
- Wire When Prototype Starts into Request to load data on open.
- Turn on **Stream** for servers that send results bit by bit, like AI text, so Result fills in as data arrives.
- In the web player, servers must allow cross-origin requests (CORS), and `http://` URLs are blocked. The desktop app has neither limit.

## Coming from Origami
Expect GraphQL Stream is now **Stream** and also handles NDJSON and server-sent events. The Boolean Error port is **Error**, and the JSON one is **Error Details**. Finished, Error Message, and Status are new, and Method adds PUT, PATCH, and DELETE.
patches.behavior:
State per loop index: `{ generation: 0, job: null, settled: null, result: <zero value of typeParam>, loading: false, error: false, errorMessage: "", status: 0, errorDetails: null, objectUrl: null }`. `job` is `{ generation, startedAt, abort }` while a request is in flight; `settled` is the finished response waiting to be applied.

Each frame:
```
let finished = false;
if (state.settled) { apply(state.settled); state.settled = null; state.job = null; finished = true; }
if (state.job && !ctx.input("disableTimeout") && ctx.time - state.job.startedAt >= 60) {
  state.job.abort?.(); state.job = null; state.generation++;
  fail(0, "The request timed out after 60 seconds.", null); finished = true;
}
if (ctx.pulsed("request")) finished = start() || finished;   // start() returns true when it fails before sending
state.loading = state.job !== null;
if (state.loading) ctx.requestNextFrame();
ctx.output("result", state.result); ctx.output("loading", state.loading);
ctx.output("error", state.error); ctx.output("errorMessage", state.errorMessage);
ctx.output("status", state.status); ctx.output("errorDetails", state.errorDetails);
if (finished) ctx.pulse("finished");
```

**start()**, in this order; any failure calls `fail(0, message, null)` on the same frame and sends nothing:
1. `url = input("url").trim()`. Empty → "Add a URL to request." Parse with `new URL(url)`; an invalid URL → "This URL isn't valid. Check for typos." A protocol other than `http:` or `https:` → "Network Request only loads http:// and https:// URLs."
2. URL Parameters must be a JSON object (or null / `{}`); otherwise → "URL Parameters must be a JSON object." For each key in insertion order: `null` is skipped, an array appends one parameter per element, an object is JSON-stringified, and anything else is `String(value)`. Parameters are appended with `url.searchParams.append`, after any query already in the URL.
3. Headers must be a JSON object; otherwise → "Headers must be a JSON object." Values follow the same stringifying rules; `null` values are skipped. A header name that isn't a valid HTTP token → "The header name "<name>" isn't valid."
4. Body is sent only when Method isn't `get`; for GET it's ignored. Media detection: a value inside Body counts as a file when it is an object with exactly one key `assetId` (string), or exactly one key `url` whose value starts with `data:` or `blob:`. Any other `{ "url": "https://…" }` stays ordinary JSON.
   - `contentType` `auto`: `multipartFormData` when Body (searched recursively) contains a file, otherwise `json`.
   - `json`: when Headers already sets `Content-Type` (case-insensitive) and Body is a string, the string is sent as-is, so people can send form-encoded or plain text. Otherwise the body is `JSON.stringify(body)` with `Content-Type: application/json`, unless Headers overrides it.
   - `multipartFormData`: Body must be a JSON object; otherwise → "Form data needs a JSON object whose keys become form fields." Each key becomes a field in insertion order: files become file parts (filename from the asset name, else `file`; MIME from the asset record or data URL), strings stay as they are, and other values are JSON-stringified. The platform sets the multipart boundary; a `Content-Type` in Headers is dropped with a one-time warning.
5. `platform.fetch` missing → "This viewer can't make network requests."
6. `state.job?.abort?.()`, then `state.generation++`, `const gen = state.generation`, and `state.job = { generation: gen, startedAt: ctx.time, abort }`. Call `platform.fetch(url, { method: METHOD, headers, body })`. On resolve or reject, store the outcome in `state.settled` only if `gen === state.generation`. Never call `ctx.output` from the callback.

**apply(outcome):**
- Rejected (transport failure, CORS, DNS): `fail(0, "Couldn't reach the server. Check the URL and your connection, and that the server allows requests from prototypes (CORS).", { message: String(reason) })`.
- `ok === false`: `fail(status, "The request failed with status <status>.", { status, body })`. `body` is the response text parsed as JSON when that works, otherwise the text truncated to 10,000 characters.
- `ok === true`: set `status`, convert the body for `typeParam`, and on success set `result`, clear `error`, `errorMessage` and `errorDetails`. A conversion failure calls `fail(status, message, { status, body })`. `result` is never cleared by a failure.
  - `json`: an empty or whitespace-only body → `null`. When the response `Content-Type` is `application/x-ndjson`, `application/ndjson` or `application/jsonl`, or when `stream` is on, the result is an array of records (below). Otherwise `JSON.parse`; failure → "The response isn't valid JSON. Switch this patch to Text to see what came back."
  - `text`: the body text, unchanged.
  - `image`, `video`, `sound`: the body bytes as a media value `{ url }`. Browsers use `URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([bytes], { type }))` and revoke the previous `objectUrl` when it's replaced; headless hosts use a `data:` URL. When the response `Content-Type` is clearly another kind (`text/*`, `application/json`), fail with "The server sent <type>, not an image." (or video, or sound). An empty media body fails with "The server sent an empty response."

**Records (json with streaming):** records are split from the text as NDJSON lines (blank lines skipped). A `text/event-stream` response splits on `data:` lines instead, skipping `[DONE]`. A `multipart/mixed` response (GraphQL incremental delivery) splits into parts, each part's JSON body being one record. Each record goes through `JSON.parse`; a record that doesn't parse fails the request with "Line <n> of the stream isn't valid JSON." Streams build arrays and never merge GraphQL patches.

- Pulses: `request` is the only pulse input. It fires on an upstream pulse or on the false→true edge of a connected boolean, so a held `true` requests once. Pulses on consecutive frames each start a new request, and each one replaces the one before it. `finished` pulses on the frame a request ends, whether it succeeded, failed, or timed out, including failures found before sending.
- Frame 0: outputs start idle (`result` is the typeParam zero value: `null` for json and media, `""` for text). A request pulse on frame 0 starts on frame 0.
- Loops: per-index state and requests. A scalar Request pulse broadcasting over a loop of URLs starts one request per index on the same frame, in index order; the platform may queue them. New indices start idle; removed indices abort their job and revoke their object URL.
- Retargeting: a new pulse while a request is in flight aborts it (when the platform honors `abort`) and ignores its result through `generation`; `loading` stays true and `finished` fires only for the newest request. Changing URL, Headers or Body without a pulse does nothing.
- Streaming (`stream` on): `loading` stays true until the response ends, and `result` updates on each frame where new data has arrived: the text so far for `text`, or the array of complete records so far for `json` (a partial trailing record waits). Media types ignore `stream`. With the current `PlatformServices.fetch` contract (no chunk callback) the stream is parsed once at the end; see Contract gaps.
- Edge cases: whitespace is trimmed from the URL. A GET Body is silently ignored. Timeout is measured in prototype seconds (`ctx.time`), so simulation is deterministic. `status` is 0 when no HTTP response arrived.
- Muted: sends nothing, ignores in-flight results, and outputs idle values (`result` zero value, `loading` false, `error` false, `errorMessage` "", `status` 0, `errorDetails` null).
- Async: follows CONVENTIONS §16.10: start on the pulse, store the outcome in state, `requestNextFrame()` while pending, apply on the next evaluate, and let `generation` discard replaced requests.
- Platform and simulation: all traffic goes through `ctx.services.platform.fetch`. The desktop host sends requests from the Electron main process (no CORS) and refuses non-HTTP schemes. The web player is subject to CORS, mixed content (an https page can't load `http://` URLs except `localhost`) and browser-forbidden headers. Headless simulation uses a host stub; without one, requests fail with the "can't make network requests" message. A stubbed response applies on the first frame after its promise settles, so hosts that step synchronously must flush pending platform promises between steps.
- Restart and dispose: abort in-flight jobs, revoke object URLs, and reset state.
- Contract gaps: `PlatformServices.fetch` has no `signal`, no response headers, no `arrayBuffer()`, and no chunk callback. Until those exist: `abort` is undefined and stale results are only ignored; the Content-Type checks are skipped; media results fall back to `{ url }` pointing at the request URL (GET with no headers only; otherwise fail with "This viewer can't download media with headers or a body yet."); and streams are parsed once at the end.
- Coming from Origami: the default type is JSON, matching Origami. Method adds PUT, PATCH and DELETE. Expect GraphQL Stream becomes Stream, which also covers NDJSON and server-sent events and produces an array of records. The Boolean Error maps to `error`, and the JSON Error maps to `errorDetails`. `finished`, `errorMessage` and `status` are new. A failed request keeps the last successful Result.

inputs.name: Request
inputs.description: Pulse to send the request. A new pulse replaces a request that's still loading.

inputs.name: URL
inputs.description: The address to load, starting with https:// or http://. Spaces at either end are ignored.

inputs.name: Method

enumOptions.name: POST
enumOptions.description: Sends Body to create something or run an action.

enumOptions.name: PATCH
enumOptions.description: Sends Body to change part of something.

enumOptions.name: DELETE
enumOptions.description: Asks the server to remove something.

inputs.description: How the request talks to the server. Most APIs use GET to read and POST to send.

inputs.name: URL Parameters
inputs.description: A JSON object whose keys and values are added to the end of the URL, like {"q": "shoes"} becoming ?q=shoes.

inputs.name: Headers
inputs.description: A JSON object of extra request headers, such as an Authorization token.

inputs.name: Body
inputs.description: The JSON to send with POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE. It's ignored for GET.

inputs.name: Content Type

enumOptions.name: Auto
enumOptions.description: Form data when Body contains an image, video, or sound; JSON otherwise.

enumOptions.name: Form Data (multipart/form-data)
enumOptions.description: Sends each key of Body as a form field, with media as file uploads.

inputs.description: How Body is packaged. Auto picks form data when Body includes media, and JSON otherwise.

inputs.name: Stream
inputs.description: When on, Result updates as data arrives instead of waiting for the whole response, for streaming APIs such as AI text generation.

inputs.name: Disable Timeout
inputs.description: When on, the request can take longer than 60 seconds. When off, a request still loading after 60 seconds fails.

outputs.name: Result
outputs.description: The response as the patch's type: JSON, text, image, video, or sound. It keeps the last good response when a later request fails.

outputs.name: Loading
outputs.description: True while a request is in progress.

outputs.name: Finished
outputs.description: Pulses when a request ends, whether it worked or failed.

outputs.name: Error
outputs.description: True when the most recent request failed.

outputs.name: Error Message
outputs.description: A plain-language reason the most recent request failed, or empty text when it worked.

outputs.name: Status
outputs.description: The HTTP status code of the last response, like 200 or 404; 0 before any response or when the server couldn't be reached.

outputs.name: Error Details
outputs.description: A JSON object describing the last failure, including the status and the server's error body; null when the last request worked.

commonMistakes: Changing the URL doesn't load anything new: requests only start on a pulse. Wire Pulse on Change on the URL, or a Tap, into Request.
Error Message says the response isn't valid JSON: the server sent a web page or plain text. Switch the patch to Text to see what came back, and check the URL.
It works in the desktop app but fails on a phone: the web player follows browser rules, so the server must allow cross-origin requests and the URL must use https://.

patches.name: Open URL
patches.statusReason: Browsers open new tabs only right after a tap or key press, and custom app schemes work only when an app handles them; headless simulation records the URL instead.
patches.summary: Opens a website, email, phone number, or app link outside the prototype when it gets a pulse.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Open URL opens a link outside the prototype when **Open** gets a pulse (a signal that's on for one frame), like a "Learn more" button that opens a web page.

- **URL** can be a website (`https://…`), an email (`mailto:…`), a phone number (`tel:…`), or another app's link scheme (`myapp://…`).
- **Opened** pulses when the link opened. **Failed** pulses when it couldn't open, and **Error Message** explains why.

On a computer, websites open in the default browser. On a phone, the link may leave the prototype and open another app.

## Tips
- Wire an Interaction patch's Tap into Open. Browsers only open new tabs right after a tap or key press, so links opened by timers are usually blocked.
- Build links from data with Add set to Text, such as a base address plus an item's id.
- Links using `javascript:`, `file:`, or `data:` are refused to keep shared prototypes safe.

## Coming from Origami
Result is named **Opened**. Failed and Error Message are new.

inputs.name: Open
inputs.description: Pulse to open the URL. Wire a Tap into it so browsers allow the new tab.

inputs.name: URL
inputs.description: The link to open: https:// for websites, mailto: for email, tel: for phone calls, or an app scheme like myapp://.

outputs.name: Opened
outputs.description: Pulses when the link opened.

outputs.name: Failed
outputs.description: Pulses when the link couldn't open, for example when the URL is empty, the browser blocked it, or the scheme isn't allowed.

outputs.name: Error Message
outputs.description: A plain-language reason the last open failed, or empty text after a link opens.

commonMistakes: Nothing opens in the web player: the pulse didn't come from a tap or key press, so the browser blocked the new tab. Trigger Open from an Interaction patch's Tap.
Failed fires with "Start the URL with https://": the URL has no scheme, like example.com. Add https:// to the front.

patches.name: WebSocket Connection
patches.statusReason: Browsers can't set WebSocket headers and block ws:// from https pages, so Headers apply only in the desktop app and the web player needs wss://.
patches.summary: Keeps a live two-way connection to a WebSocket server open while Connect is on, for sending and receiving messages instantly.
patches.docs:
## How it works
WebSocket Connection keeps a live, two-way line open to a server, so a prototype can send and receive messages instantly. Use it for chat, live cursors, multiplayer games, or a script that controls the prototype remotely.

- **Connect** opens the connection while it's on and closes it when it turns off.
- **URL** is the server address, starting with `wss://` (or `ws://` for a server on your own computer).
- **Connection** is the handle you wire into WebSocket Send and WebSocket Receive. One connection can feed as many of each as you like.
- **Connected** is true while the line is open. **Connecting** is true while it's being set up.
- **Error** and **Error Message** report the latest problem, including failed sends.

The connection doesn't retry by itself. Turn Connect off and on again to reconnect.

## Tips
- Drive Connect from a Switch so a button can start and stop the connection.
- Show Connected on a status dot so you can tell when messages will get through.
- **Headers** (advanced) only reach the server in the desktop app, because browsers don't allow them. In the web player, put tokens in the URL instead.

## Coming from Origami
Origami's text Error output is **Error Message** here. Error (a true/false value) and Connecting are new.
patches.behavior:
State per instance (inputs are `wholeLoop`, so there's one connection per patch): `{ socket: null, phase: "idle", target: null, error: false, errorMessage: "", warnedLoop: false, warnedHeaders: false, events: [] }`. `phase` is `"idle" | "connecting" | "open" | "ended"`. `target` is the `{ url, headersKey }` the socket was opened with. `events` holds socket callbacks (open, message, close, error) queued since the last frame.

Shared per runtime: a module-level `WeakMap<RuntimeServices, Map<string, ConnectionRecord>>`, keyed by `"<componentPath>/<patchId>"`. A record is `{ socket, phase, frame, messages: Message[], sendError: string | null, sendOk: boolean }`, where `Message = { text: string, parsed?: { ok: boolean, value: unknown } }`. `parsed` is filled lazily the first time a JSON receiver reads the message, so it's parsed at most once. The `connection` output is a frozen handle `{ kind: "webSocket", key }` that WebSocket Send and WebSocket Receive use to find the record.

Each frame:
```
const connect = items("connect")[0] ?? false, url = String(items("url")[0] ?? "").trim(), headers = items("headers")[0] ?? {};
warn once if any input has more than one item ("WebSocket Connection can't be looped; using the first item").
record.messages = []; record.frame = ctx.frame;
drain state.events in arrival order:
  open    → phase = "open"; error = false; errorMessage = ""
  message → record.messages.push({ text })          (binary frames are decoded as UTF-8, replacing invalid bytes)
  close   → if phase !== "idle": phase = "ended"; socket = null;
            code 1000 or 1001 → error = false, errorMessage = "The server closed the connection."
            otherwise → error = true, errorMessage = "The connection was lost (code <code>)." plus the reason when present
  error   → error = true; errorMessage = <platform message> or "Couldn't connect. Check the URL and that the server is running."
if (record.sendError !== null) { error = true; errorMessage = record.sendError; record.sendError = null; }
else if (record.sendOk && phase === "open" && error) { error = false; errorMessage = ""; }
record.sendOk = false;
const wanted = connect && url !== "";
const next = { url, headersKey: stableStringify(headers) };
if (!wanted) closeSocket();                                          // phase = "idle"; error is kept
else if (phase === "idle" || rose(connect) || !sameTarget(state.target, next)) { closeSocket(); openSocket(next); }
ctx.output("connection", handle); ctx.output("connected", phase === "open");
ctx.output("connecting", phase === "connecting"); ctx.output("error", error); ctx.output("errorMessage", errorMessage);
if (phase === "connecting" || phase === "open") ctx.requestNextFrame();
```

**openSocket(target):** clear `error` and `errorMessage`, then:
- `http:` and `https:` URLs become `ws:` and `wss:`. Any other scheme fails → "WebSocket URLs start with wss:// or ws://."
- Headers must be a JSON object; otherwise → "Headers must be a JSON object." Values follow Network Request's stringifying rules.
- `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` (case-insensitive) is split on commas into `protocols`.
- Call `platform.webSocket(url, { protocols, headers })`. A missing service fails → "This viewer can't open WebSockets."
- Set `phase = "connecting"`, store `target`, and attach callbacks that only push to `state.events`. They check a generation number so callbacks from a replaced socket are ignored.
- A failure here sets `phase = "ended"`, `error = true`, and the message.

**closeSocket():** when a socket exists, call `socket.close(1000, "closed by prototype")`, detach callbacks, and set `socket = null` and `phase = "idle"`.

- Pulses: none. `connect` is a state: the socket stays open while it's true.
- Frame 0: an authored `connect: true` opens the socket on frame 0; `connected` becomes true on the first frame after the open event arrives.
- Loops: all inputs are `wholeLoop`, so the patch never replicates. It uses the first item of each input and warns once per restart when an input has more than one item.
- Retargeting: changing URL or Headers while Connect is on closes the old socket and opens a new one on the same frame. Typing a URL character by character reconnects on each change; wire it through Sample and Hold if that matters.
- No automatic reconnect: after an error or a server close, `phase` stays `"ended"` until Connect goes false→true or the URL or Headers change.
- Errors: `error` and `errorMessage` report the latest problem with connecting, sending (from WebSocket Send via `record.sendError`) or the connection dropping. Starting a new connection clears them, and so does a successful send while the connection is open. Turning Connect off keeps the last error visible.
- Edge cases: an empty URL with Connect on stays idle and reports nothing. A backlog of more than 10,000 messages in one frame drops the oldest, with one warning per restart.
- Muted: closes any socket and outputs idle values (`connection` null, `connected` false, `connecting` false, `error` false, `errorMessage` "").
- Async: socket callbacks only enqueue `state.events`; outputs change only inside `evaluate`.
- Platform and simulation: the desktop host opens sockets from the Electron main process, where Headers are sent. The web player uses the browser `WebSocket`: only `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` can be honored, and other headers are ignored with one warning per restart ("Browsers don't let prototypes set WebSocket headers; Headers only apply in the desktop app. Put a token in the URL instead."). An https page can't open `ws://` except to `localhost`, and that case fails with "Browsers block ws:// from secure pages. Use wss://." Headless simulation uses a host stub (for example an echo server); without one it fails with the "can't open WebSockets" message.
- Restart and dispose: close the socket with code 1000, delete the record, and reset state. `updateDocument` keeps the socket open when the patch's type is unchanged.
- Contract gap: `PlatformServices` has no WebSocket member (CONVENTIONS §19.7). Until it does, hosts attach `webSocket(url, { protocols, headers })` to the platform object. It returns `{ send(text), close(code, reason), bufferedAmount, onopen, onmessage(text), onclose(code, reason), onerror(message) }`, and the patch reads it through a local structural type. The connection handle travels on an `any` port until a `connection` value type exists.
- Coming from Origami: Origami's text Error output is Error Message. Error (a boolean) and Connecting are new. Like Origami, the patch can't be looped and doesn't reconnect by itself.

inputs.name: Connect
inputs.description: When on, opens the connection and keeps it open; turning it off closes it. Turn it off and on again to reconnect.

inputs.name: URL
inputs.description: The server address, starting with wss:// (secure) or ws://. Changing it while connected reconnects to the new address.

inputs.name: Headers
inputs.description: A JSON object of headers sent when connecting, such as an Authorization token. Only the desktop app can send them.

outputs.name: Connection
outputs.description: A handle to this connection. Wire it into WebSocket Send and WebSocket Receive.

outputs.name: Connected
outputs.description: True while the connection is open and messages can travel.

outputs.name: Connecting
outputs.description: True while the connection is being set up.

outputs.name: Error
outputs.description: True when the latest attempt to connect or send had a problem.

outputs.name: Error Message
outputs.description: A plain-language description of the latest problem, or empty text when there's none.

commonMistakes: Connected never turns on in the web player: the URL uses ws:// from a secure page, or the server needs a header browsers can't send. Use wss:// and put tokens in the URL.
The connection drops and never comes back: it doesn't retry by itself. Turn Connect off and on again, for example with a Switch.

patches.name: WebSocket Send
patches.summary: Sends a text or JSON message over a WebSocket connection when it gets a pulse.
patches.docs:
## How it works
WebSocket Send sends a message to a server when **Send** gets a pulse (a signal that's on for one frame). It works together with a WebSocket Connection patch.

- **Connection** comes from a WebSocket Connection patch.
- **Message** is what gets sent. Right-click to choose Text or JSON; JSON is sent as text the server can parse.
- **Sent** pulses when the message went out.

If the connection isn't open, nothing is sent, and the problem appears on the connection's Error Message.

## Tips
- Use several Send patches on one connection, such as a Text one for pings and a JSON one for events.
- If Message is a loop, each item goes out as its own message. Use Loop to Array to send them as one list.
- To stream a changing value, like a dragged position, wire Pulse on Change into Send.

## Coming from Origami
Sent is new.

inputs.name: Connection
inputs.description: The Connection output of a WebSocket Connection patch.

inputs.name: Send
inputs.description: Pulse to send the current Message.

inputs.name: Message
inputs.description: The text or JSON to send. A loop sends each item as its own message.

outputs.name: Sent
outputs.description: Pulses when a message was handed to the connection. It doesn't fire when the connection isn't open.

commonMistakes: The connection's Error Message says it isn't connected yet: Send pulsed before the connection opened, often on the first frame. Wire Connected through a Pulse patch's Turned On to send once the line is open.
Editing Message doesn't send anything: messages only go out on a pulse. Wire a Tap or Pulse on Change into Send.
The server gets several messages instead of one list: Message is a loop, so each item is sent separately. Convert it with Loop to Array first.

patches.name: WebSocket Receive
patches.summary: Outputs the text or JSON messages a server sends over a WebSocket connection, and pulses when each new one arrives.
patches.docs:
## How it works
WebSocket Receive listens on a WebSocket connection and outputs the messages the server sends. It works together with a WebSocket Connection patch.

- **Connection** comes from a WebSocket Connection patch.
- Right-click to choose **Text** or **JSON**. A JSON receiver ignores messages that aren't valid JSON, and a Text receiver gets everything as text.
- **Message** holds the latest message until the next one arrives.
- **Messages** lists every message that arrived this frame, which matters when a server sends several at once.
- **Received** pulses (a signal that's on for one frame) whenever a new message arrives, even when it repeats the last one.

You can use as many Receive patches on one connection as you like, and each one sees every message.

## Tips
- Bind Message to a layer for values that replace each other, like a live score or a cursor position.
- For chat feeds and other lists, add from Messages when Received pulses so bursts don't lose items.
- Pass a JSON Message through Value for Key to read one field.

## Coming from Origami
Message is always a single value. Several messages in one frame come out on the new **Messages** output, and **Received** is new.

inputs.name: Connection
inputs.description: The Connection output of a WebSocket Connection patch.

outputs.name: Message
outputs.description: The latest message that matches this patch's type, held until the next one arrives.

outputs.name: Messages
outputs.description: Every matching message that arrived this frame, in order, as a loop; empty on frames with no messages.

outputs.name: Received
outputs.description: Pulses on each frame where at least one matching message arrived, even if it repeats the previous one.

commonMistakes: A chat list skips messages: two arrived in the same frame and Message only holds the latest. Add items from Messages when Received pulses.
A JSON receiver never updates: the server sends plain text that isn't valid JSON. Switch the patch to Text to see what arrives.
Repeated identical messages don't trigger anything: Pulse on Change only fires when the value differs. Use Received, which pulses for every message.

patch live webSocketConnection connect=true url="wss://example.com/live"
patch inbox webSocketReceive<json> connection←live.connection
patch tally counter increase←inbox.received

patches.name: Base64 Encode
patches.summary: Turns text, JSON, an image, or a sound into base64 text for sending inside requests, links, or JSON.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Base64 Encode turns data into base64: plain text made only of letters, digits, and a few symbols, so it can travel safely inside JSON, URLs, and request headers.

- Right-click to choose what **Value** is: Text, JSON, Image, or Sound.
- **Base64** is the encoded text. It updates whenever Value changes.
- **Loading** is true while a large image or sound is still being read and encoded.
- **URL Safe** (advanced) swaps `+` and `/` for `-` and `_` and drops the `=` padding, so the result can sit inside a link.
- **Queue** (advanced) encodes every value in order instead of skipping to the newest one when values change faster than encoding finishes.

## Tips
- Some APIs want images uploaded as base64 inside a JSON body. Encode the image, then put Base64 into the request's Body.
- Basic authentication headers use `Basic ` followed by the base64 of `username:password`.
- Base64 is about a third larger than the original data, and anyone can decode it. It isn't encryption.

## Coming from Origami
This patch was called Encode. Its Text output is named **Base64**, and URL Safe, Error, and Error Message are new.
patches.behavior:
State per loop index: `{ generation: 0, job: null, queue: [], base64: "", loading: false, error: false, errorMessage: "", started: false }`. A job is `{ generation, value, urlSafe, bytes: Uint8Array | null, offset, parts: string[], reading: boolean }`.

Each frame, per loop index:
```
if (!state.started || ctx.changed("value") || ctx.changed("urlSafe")) { state.started = true; submit({ value: ctx.input("value"), urlSafe: ctx.input("urlSafe") }); }
let finishedThisFrame = false;
if (state.job && state.job.bytes) finishedThisFrame = advance(state.job);   // encodes up to 1,500,000 bytes (a multiple of 3) this frame
if (!state.job && !finishedThisFrame && state.queue.length > 0) start(state.queue.shift());   // the next queued job starts the frame after one finishes
state.loading = state.job !== null;
if (state.loading) ctx.requestNextFrame();
ctx.output("base64", state.base64); ctx.output("loading", state.loading);
ctx.output("error", state.error); ctx.output("errorMessage", state.errorMessage);
```

**submit(input):** with `queue` off, discard the current job and any queued inputs (`generation++`) and `start(input)` now. With `queue` on, `start(input)` when idle; otherwise push it onto `queue`. The queue holds at most 100 inputs; when it overflows, the oldest queued input is dropped with one warning per restart.

**start(input):** `generation++`, then create the job and get its bytes:
- `text`: `new TextEncoder().encode(String(value ?? ""))`, the UTF-8 bytes.
- `json`: `TextEncoder` over `JSON.stringify(value === undefined ? null : value)`: compact, with keys in the value's own order. A JSON string value therefore encodes with its quotes.
- `image`, `sound`: `null` → finish with `""` and no error. `{ url: "data:…;base64,<payload>" }` → use the payload directly: normalize it as Base64 Decode does and skip the byte pass. Any other data URL is percent-decoded into bytes. `{ assetId }` resolves through `ctx.services.resolveAssetUrl`; a missing asset finishes with the error "The image asset is missing." (or sound). Other URLs (`blob:`, `http:`, `https:`, asset URLs) are read through the platform byte reader, and the job waits with `reading: true`. The result is stored only when `job.generation === state.generation`. A read failure finishes with "Couldn't read the image data." (or sound). No re-encoding happens: the output is the file's original bytes (PNG, JPEG, MP3…).

**advance(job):** append `base64(bytes.subarray(offset, offset + 1_500_000))` to `parts` and advance `offset`. When `offset >= bytes.length`, finish: `base64 = parts.join("")`; when `urlSafe` is on, replace `+` with `-` and `/` with `_` and remove trailing `=`. Then set `error = false`, `errorMessage = ""`, and `job = null`, and return true. Inputs up to 1,500,000 bytes finish on the frame they're submitted.

- Pulses: none. Work starts when Value or URL Safe changes (`ctx.changed`) and on the first evaluation.
- Frame 0: text and JSON inputs up to 1.5 MB are encoded on frame 0, so `base64` is ready immediately and `loading` stays false.
- Loops: per-index state, jobs and queues. New indices encode on their first evaluation; removed indices drop their jobs.
- Retargeting: with Queue off, the newest input wins and a stale media read is ignored through `generation`. With Queue on, each input finishes in order, and its result shows for at least one frame before the next job starts. `base64` keeps the previous result while a job runs; it never shows partial output.
- Edge cases: empty text encodes to `""`. Encoding text or JSON can't fail. Output is RFC 4648 base64 with no line breaks and no `data:` prefix.
- Muted: no work; outputs `base64` "", `loading` false, `error` false, `errorMessage` "".
- Async: media byte reads resolve into the job, never into outputs directly; `requestNextFrame()` runs while a job exists.
- Platform and simulation: text and JSON behave identically everywhere. Media reads use host byte access: in browsers `fetch(url).arrayBuffer()` on asset, blob and http URLs, and in headless hosts the project's asset files.
- Restart and dispose: discard jobs and queues and reset state; frame 0 encodes again.
- Contract gap: `RuntimeServices` can't read bytes (`PlatformServices.fetch` exposes only `text()`). Proposed: `PlatformServices.readBytes?: (url: string) => Promise<Uint8Array>`, or `arrayBuffer()` on the fetch response. Until then only `data:` media values encode; others finish with "This viewer can't read media data yet."
- Coming from Origami: the unnamed input is `value` and the Text output is `base64`. URL Safe, Error and Error Message are new. Like Origami, Video isn't a type.

inputs.name: Value
inputs.description: The text, JSON, image, or sound to encode, depending on the patch's type.

inputs.name: URL Safe
inputs.description: When on, uses - and _ instead of + and / and removes = padding, so the result can go inside a URL.

inputs.name: Queue
inputs.description: When on, every new value is encoded in order. When off, a new value replaces one that's still encoding.

outputs.name: Base64
outputs.description: The encoded base64 text, without line breaks or a data: prefix. It keeps the previous result while new work is loading.

outputs.name: Loading
outputs.description: True while a large value or a media file is still being encoded.

outputs.name: Error
outputs.description: True when the image or sound couldn't be read.

outputs.name: Error Message
outputs.description: A plain-language reason encoding failed, or empty text when it worked.

commonMistakes: The server rejects a Basic authentication header: the whole header, including the word Basic, was encoded. Encode only username:password, then join "Basic " in front with Add set to Text.
The result decodes to text wrapped in quotes: the patch is set to JSON while Value is plain text, so it's encoded as a JSON string. Switch the patch to Text.
A link with base64 in it breaks: standard base64 uses + and /, which URLs treat specially. Turn on URL Safe.

patch share_link add<text>[2] value1="https://example.com/play?s=" value2←encode_state.base64

patches.name: Base64 Decode
patches.summary: Turns base64 text back into text, JSON, an image, or a sound.
patches.docs:
## How it works
Base64 Decode turns base64 text (letters, digits, and a few symbols that stand in for data) back into the original text, JSON, image, or sound. APIs often send small images or payloads this way inside JSON.

- **Base64** is the text to decode. A `data:…;base64,` prefix, line breaks, and the URL-safe `-` and `_` characters are all fine.
- Right-click to choose what **Output** is: Text, JSON, Image, or Sound.
- **Loading** is true while a very large payload is still being decoded.
- **Error** and **Error Message** explain what went wrong, such as text that isn't base64 or data that isn't an image.
- **Queue** (advanced) decodes every value in order instead of skipping to the newest one.

## Tips
- Connect an Image Output straight to an Image layer's Image property.
- Pull the base64 field out of a JSON response with Value for Key before decoding it.
- If a JSON decode fails, switch to Text to see what the data really contains.

## Coming from Origami
This patch was called Decode. Its Text input is named **Base64**. Error and Error Message are new.
patches.behavior:
State per loop index: `{ generation: 0, job: null, queue: [], output: <zero value of typeParam>, loading: false, error: false, errorMessage: "", started: false }`. A job is `{ generation, b64: string, mime: string | null, offset, chunks: Uint8Array[] }`.

Each frame, per loop index:
```
if (!state.started || ctx.changed("base64")) { state.started = true; submit(ctx.input("base64")); }
let finishedThisFrame = false;
if (state.job) finishedThisFrame = advance(state.job);   // decodes up to 2,000,000 characters (a multiple of 4) this frame
if (!state.job && !finishedThisFrame && state.queue.length > 0) start(state.queue.shift());
state.loading = state.job !== null;
if (state.loading) ctx.requestNextFrame();
ctx.output("output", state.output); ctx.output("loading", state.loading);
ctx.output("error", state.error); ctx.output("errorMessage", state.errorMessage);
```

**submit / queue:** identical to Base64 Encode: Queue off means the newest input wins; Queue on means FIFO, at most 100 entries, and each result shows for at least one frame.

**start(text) normalizes synchronously:**
1. `s = String(text ?? "").trim()`.
2. When `s` matches `^data:([^,;]*)((?:;[^,;]*)*);base64,` (case-insensitive), remember the MIME type and strip the prefix. A `data:` URL without `;base64` → fail "This is a data URL, but it isn't base64."
3. Remove all whitespace, map `-` to `+` and `_` to `/`, and strip trailing `=`. The rest must match `^[A-Za-z0-9+/]*$` and its length can't be `≡ 1 (mod 4)`; otherwise → fail "This isn't valid base64 text." Re-pad with `=` to a multiple of 4.
4. Empty after normalizing → finish with the zero value and no error.
5. `image` and `sound` finish right away, without a byte pass. Decode only the first 64 characters to sniff the format. MIME comes from the data URL when it's `image/*` or `audio/*` (matching the type), otherwise from magic bytes:
   - images: `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A` → `image/png`; `FF D8 FF` → `image/jpeg`; `GIF87a` or `GIF89a` → `image/gif`; `RIFF`, 4 bytes, `WEBP` → `image/webp`; `BM` → `image/bmp`; `ftyp` at offset 4 with brand `avif` or `avis` → `image/avif`; text starting with `<svg`, or `<?xml` followed by `<svg` (after optional BOM and whitespace) → `image/svg+xml`.
   - sounds: `ID3` → `audio/mpeg`; `FF` then `(b1 & 0xF6) === 0xF0` → `audio/aac`; `FF` then `(b1 & 0xE0) === 0xE0` → `audio/mpeg`; `RIFF`, 4 bytes, `WAVE` → `audio/wav`; `OggS` → `audio/ogg`; `fLaC` → `audio/flac`; `ftyp` at offset 4 → `audio/mp4`.
   - no match → fail "The decoded data isn't an image (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, BMP, or SVG)." or "…isn't a sound (MP3, AAC, WAV, OGG, FLAC, or M4A)."
   - success: `output = { url: "data:<mime>;base64,<normalized>" }`.
6. `text` and `json` create a job that decodes bytes in slices.

**advance(job)** decodes the next slice of at most 2,000,000 characters into bytes. After the last slice, concatenate the bytes and finish:
- `text`: `new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: false }).decode(bytes)`, which replaces invalid byte sequences with U+FFFD.
- `json`: decode the text the same way, then `JSON.parse`; a failure → fail "The decoded text isn't valid JSON. Switch this patch to Text to see what's inside."
- Finishing sets `output`, `error = false`, `errorMessage = ""`, `job = null`.

**fail(message):** `output = zero value`, `error = true`, `errorMessage = message`, `job = null`. The output always matches the current input, so stale results never show for different text.

- Pulses: none. Work starts when Base64 changes and on the first evaluation.
- Frame 0: inputs up to 2,000,000 characters and every media input finish on frame 0, so `loading` stays false.
- Loops: per-index state, jobs and queues.
- Retargeting: while a job is still slicing, `output` keeps the previous result and `loading` is true. With Queue off, a new input discards the unfinished job.
- Edge cases: standard and URL-safe alphabets, missing padding, embedded line breaks and `data:` prefixes are all accepted. Never outputs `undefined`: failures emit the zero value (`""` for text, `null` for json, image and sound).
- Muted: no work; outputs the zero value, `loading` false, `error` false, `errorMessage` "".
- Platform and simulation: pure computation that behaves identically everywhere. Media results are `data:` URLs, so no object URLs need releasing.
- Restart and dispose: discard jobs and queues and reset state; frame 0 decodes again.
- Coming from Origami: this patch was called Decode. Its Text input is `base64` and its unnamed output is `output`. Error and Error Message are new, data URLs and URL-safe text are accepted, and a failed decode clears the output instead of leaving it undefined.

inputs.name: Base64
inputs.description: The base64 text to decode. A data: prefix, line breaks, and URL-safe characters are accepted.

inputs.name: Queue
inputs.description: When on, every new value is decoded in order. When off, a new value replaces one that's still decoding.

outputs.name: Output
outputs.description: The decoded text, JSON, image, or sound, depending on the patch's type. It's empty (or null) when decoding fails.

outputs.name: Loading
outputs.description: True while a very large value is still being decoded.

outputs.name: Error
outputs.description: True when the text isn't valid base64 or doesn't decode to the patch's type.

outputs.name: Error Message
outputs.description: A plain-language reason decoding failed, or empty text when it worked.

commonMistakes: Error Message says the text isn't valid base64: extra characters came along, such as quotes, a label, or a whole JSON object. Pass only the base64 field, for example through Value for Key.
The image never appears: the patch is still set to Text or JSON. Right-click it and choose Image.
JSON Output is null with an error: the data decodes to text that isn't JSON. Switch the patch to Text to see what's inside.
